experiment: Curiosity-driven range-object inspection with persistent novelty memory
physics: MuJoCo native; 60 simulated seconds per seed
robot_control: reference V5 only, not PPO checkpoint
sensors: 23 idealized planar range beams; world pose from simulator truth
object_sensing: range-endpoint clusters without simulator object IDs; static box obstacles
limitations: Object hypotheses may split or merge because they rely on sparse planar range beams
Object inspection is safe observation at distance, not touching, manipulation, or learning new motor skills
Memory adapts object priority from outcomes; no semantic vision or end-to-end RL of object interaction
World pose and contact point are provided by simulation, not physical sensors
Success on 12 fixed random seeds is not a safety guarantee
Curiosity reduces space coverage compared with pure frontier exploration
